answer.summary: No prior research supports non-feature-based memory indicators in agent systems under controlled, low-variation conditions without external validation or feature vectors.
answer.content: The review of Kumar et al., 2024, across Sections 2.4, 3.3, 4.1, 5.2, and 6.1 reveals consistent absence of explicit or implicit evidence for observable, non-feature-based memory indicators such as thematic drift, semantic coherence, internal consistency, or metacognitive awareness in the absence of external cues or validation. All reported behaviors remain tied to structured memory mechanisms or external feedback loops. The lack of temporal or behavioral continuity under stable input conditions suggests current models do not demonstrate emergent memory properties beyond feature-vector dependence.
